name: Study & Space
summary: Learn the vocabulary, read the core books, prepare a corner of the shop and a low planing beam before buying anything.

milestones.title: Read Odate's Japanese Woodworking Tools (tool chapters)
Watch a full kanna setup and a full chisel-sharpening video end to end
Set up work area + low planing beam on the existing workbench

name: Starter Kit & Sharpening
summary: Buy the minimum kit, flatten the stones, and learn to sharpen chisels and set up a kanna. Nothing else matters until the edges are sharp.
budgetNote: Starter kit (~$374) + Atoma #400 diamond plate for flattening stones and backs ($91).

milestones.title: Flatten the chisel backs (ura-oshi) on 3 nomi
Kanna setup: fit the blade, tune the dai, take a full-length shaving
Saw drills: 20 square crosscuts and 20 rip cuts to a line

name: First Joints
summary: Layout with sashigane and marking knife, then the basic family of joints in softwood until they fit off the saw.
budgetNote: Practice lumber (estimate ~$80) + Fujihiro mortise chisel ($122.90) + Tajima sumitsubo ($54.98).

milestones.title: Half-lap (ai-gaki) — 5 in a row that close with hand pressure

name: First Projects
summary: Turn practice into things I'll use every day: a stone stand, a Japanese tool box, and a small stool.

milestones.title: Dogu-bako tool box with sliding lid
Small stool with through tenons and wedges

name: Splices & Connections
summary: The classic timber splices and connections that make Japanese carpentry what it is.

name: Kumiko
summary: Precision small-stock work: lattice panels built from thin strips with no glue or nails.

name: Advanced Joinery
summary: The showpieces: the rabbeted oblique scarf and the three-way corner joint.

milestones.title: Capstone: small display piece combining 3 joints
